open_points.subject: AuditEntry lifecycle across restore
open_points.text: “a restore from an older backup does not lower [the last number written]” contradicts “written -> erased by the owner's dated erasure” and “Only the owner erases it”
open_points.question: Can restoring an older backup remove AuditEntries written after that backup, or must those entries survive the restore as well as the sequence high-water mark?
options: Restore may remove the later entries, adding restore as another AuditEntry lifecycle transition
All written AuditEntries must survive or be recovered during restore
A restore that would omit later AuditEntries is refused
open_points.default_guess: Restore may remove post-backup entries, but their sequence numbers remain consumed and are never reused.

open_points.subject: Audit sequence persistence
open_points.text: “the last number written is held in the instance marks outside the store” conflicts with State 0's “One instance, one store”
open_points.question: Are the instance marks part of Registry's one durable store, or does Registry now own a second durable persistence location outside that store?
options: Instance marks are a second durable persistence location
Instance marks are logically part of the one Registry store
The high-water mark remains in the store and may fall back on restore
open_points.default_guess: Treat the instance marks as a second durable persistence location owned by Registry.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure facts in instance marks
open_points.text: “also held in the instance marks outside the store” does not say whether the marks hold the whole MigrationClosure or only the fact that an import succeeded
open_points.question: After restoring a backup that predates the import, where do the closure's instant, acting principal, confirmation id and accepted-file digest come from?
options: The instance marks mirror every MigrationClosure fact
The marks hold only a closed boolean and the other closure facts may be absent
The marks hold an identity or digest from which the full closure is recovered elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: The instance marks mirror the complete MigrationClosure and become authoritative when the store lacks or disagrees with it.

open_points.subject: Migration closure versus imported models after restore
open_points.text: “a restore from an older backup does not lose [the MigrationClosure]” is silent about the Projects, Customers, Rooms and ArtifactPointers created by the successful import
open_points.question: If a restored backup predates the import, must the imported models also survive or be recovered, or may Registry retain the closure and refuse another import while those models are absent?
options: The imported models must survive or be recovered together with the closure
The closure survives even if the imported models are lost, and import remains closed
The closure is cleared when the corresponding imported models are absent, allowing the import again
A backup predating the successful import cannot be restored
open_points.default_guess: The imported models must be recovered together with the surviving closure; Registry must not expose a closed migration with its imported records missing.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure persistence location
open_points.text: “also held in the instance marks outside the store” conflicts with State 0's “One instance, one store”
open_points.question: Are the instance marks part of Registry's one durable store, or does MigrationClosure now exist in a second durable persistence location?
options: Instance marks are a second durable persistence location
Instance marks are logically part of the one Registry store
MigrationClosure is held only in the store and can be rolled back by restore
open_points.default_guess: Treat the instance marks as a second durable persistence location owned by Registry.
